title: Government policy and legal regulation
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, social, legal and political influences, is a broad Year 11 overview of external influences, while the new point looks specifically at how particular laws and regulations shape operations at Year 12 depth, so it is narrower and deeper and needs its own point.

draft.title: Government policy and legal regulation
card: Governments make laws and policies that businesses must follow. These set limits on how operations are run, from the factory floor to the finished product.
laws that require a safe workplace, such as safe equipment, training and a way to report hazards. In NSW this is the work health and safety legislation.
laws that limit pollution and waste and require approvals for some activities. A business that breaks them can be fined.
laws such as the Australian Consumer Law, which require goods to be safe and as described. Industry rules add extra standards, such as food handling or licences to operate.
draft.remember: Laws on safety, environment, consumers and industry rules shape how operations are run.

a.q: A bakery must install a safe guard on its dough mixer and train staff to use it. Which type of regulation requires this?
a.why: Safe equipment and training for workers come under work safety law. Consumer protection law is the tempting option, but it covers the goods sold to customers, not the machines staff use.
a.clue: Who is the rule protecting: workers or buyers?

b.q: Dana's factory in Newcastle makes toys. A new law says toys must meet safety standards and be as described on the label. Which area of regulation does this affect, and how does it shape operations?
opts: Consumer protection, so products are tested before sale
Work safety, so staff need extra training on machines
Environmental law, so the factory must cut its waste
Industry rules, so the factory needs a licence to open
b.why: Rules on product safety and accurate labels are consumer protection. They shape operations by requiring checks on the toys before they reach customers. Work safety is tempting because the toys are made in a factory, but the law here protects buyers, not staff.
b.clue: The law is about the product that customers receive.

b.best: Consumer protection, so products are tested before sale
